$comment: Curated explanations for common macOS processes and third-party helpers. Keyed by executable basename, matched case-insensitively. kill: safe = can be quit without harm; restarts = launchd relaunches it; avoid = killing breaks the session or the app.

Activity Monitor.normal: A few percent CPU while open; that is the cost of polling.

Adobe Desktop Service.normal: Low CPU; bursts while checking for updates.
Adobe Desktop Service.worry: Constant CPU is a known Creative Cloud problem.
Adobe Desktop Service.check: Quit Creative Cloud from its menu bar item.

amfid.what: Apple Mobile File Integrity: verifies code signatures at launch.

AnyDesk.normal: Idle unless a session is active.
AnyDesk.worry: A session active when you are not using it means someone else is.
AnyDesk.check: Quit it when not in use; review its connection log.

apsd.what: Apple Push Notification service client. Keeps one connection open for all notifications.

Arc Helper (Renderer).worry: One at high CPU is a heavy page.

ARDAgent.worry: Present on a Mac that is not managed with Remote Desktop.
ARDAgent.check: System Settings, General, Sharing, Remote Management.

AudioComponentRegistrar.what: Scans and registers Audio Units (plug-ins) for audio apps.
AudioComponentRegistrar.normal: Brief bursts when an audio app opens.
AudioComponentRegistrar.worry: Constant CPU points at a plug-in that fails to load and is retried.

bash.what: The Bourne-again shell, used by scripts and older tools.
bash.normal: Idle unless a script is running.

bird.normal: Busy after edits in iCloud Drive or Desktop and Documents sync.
bird.worry: Constant high CPU with iCloud status stuck.
bird.check: System Settings, Apple Account, iCloud Drive; sign out and in if it stays stuck.

bluetoothd.normal: Low CPU while devices are connected.
bluetoothd.worry: High CPU usually points at a flaky peripheral.

Brave Browser Helper (Renderer).worry: One at high CPU is a heavy page.

browser_crashpad_handler.what: A Chromium-based browser's crash reporter, waiting for a crash.

bun.what: The Bun JavaScript runtime, running a script or a dev server.

caddy.check: The Network tab shows its listeners.

CCXProcess.what: Creative Cloud's content and library service.

cfprefsd.what: Preferences daemon. Reads and writes app defaults for every process.
cfprefsd.worry: An app writing preferences in a tight loop shows up here.
cfprefsd.check: Find the app with high CPU alongside it.

ChatGPT for Chrome.what: The ChatGPT Chrome extension's native host.

ChatGPTHelper.what: The ChatGPT desktop app's helper (screen and app context features).
ChatGPTHelper.worry: Busy when the app is closed.
ChatGPTHelper.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Screen and System Audio Recording.

chrome-native-host.what: A native messaging host that a Chrome extension talks to (password managers, download tools).
chrome-native-host.worry: A host you cannot match to an extension you installed.
chrome-native-host.check: Follow the path to the app that owns it; chrome://extensions lists the extension side.

chrome_crashpad_handler.what: Chrome's crash reporter, waiting for a crash to report.

chronod.worry: Constant CPU points at a widget refreshing too often.
chronod.check: Remove widgets you do not use.

clang.what: The C, C++ and Objective-C compiler.
clang.normal: High CPU during a build; gone afterwards.

Claude.what: The Claude desktop app's main process.

claude bg-pty-host.what: Claude Code's terminal host for background sessions.

claude bg-spare.what: A pre-warmed spare Claude Code process for the next background job.

Claude Helper.what: A Claude desktop app helper (network or utility process).

Claude Helper (Plugin).what: Hosts Claude desktop extensions and MCP connectors.

Claude Helper (Renderer).normal: Low CPU; spikes while a long response streams.

cloudd.what: CloudKit daemon. Syncs app data (Photos, Notes, Messages in iCloud, third-party apps) with iCloud.

cloudphotod.what: Syncs your Photos library with iCloud Photos.
cloudphotod.normal: Network and CPU while syncing; idle otherwise.
cloudphotod.worry: Constant activity with nothing new to sync.
cloudphotod.check: Photos, Settings, iCloud, and check the sync status at the bottom of the Library view.

CloudTelemetryService.what: A third-party telemetry service (the parent app tells you whose).
CloudTelemetryService.worry: One you cannot match to an installed app.
CloudTelemetryService.check: Follow the path to the owning app.

CMFSyncAgent.what: Syncs Screen Time and family settings across devices.

Code.normal: Low CPU; the helpers do the work.

Code - Insiders Helper.what: A Visual Studio Code Insiders helper process (utility, shared or extension host).
Code - Insiders Helper.normal: Low CPU; extension hosts spike while an extension works.
Code - Insiders Helper.worry: An extension host at high CPU means one extension is busy or looping.
Code - Insiders Helper.check: In VS Code, run Developer: Show Running Extensions.

Code - Insiders Helper (GPU).what: GPU process for Visual Studio Code Insiders.

Code - Insiders Helper (Plugin).what: Hosts Visual Studio Code Insiders extensions.
Code - Insiders Helper (Plugin).worry: Sustained high CPU means one extension is busy.
Code - Insiders Helper (Plugin).check: In VS Code, run Developer: Show Running Extensions.

Code - Insiders Helper (Renderer).what: Renders a Visual Studio Code Insiders window.
Code - Insiders Helper (Renderer).normal: Low CPU; spikes while typing in a large file.
Code - Insiders Helper (Renderer).worry: Sustained high CPU usually comes from a language extension.
Code - Insiders Helper (Renderer).check: In VS Code, run Developer: Show Running Extensions.

Code Helper.what: A Visual Studio Code helper process (utility, shared or extension host).
Code Helper.normal: Low CPU; extension hosts spike while an extension works.
Code Helper.worry: An extension host at high CPU means one extension is busy or looping.
Code Helper.check: In VS Code, run Developer: Show Running Extensions.

Code Helper (GPU).what: GPU process for Visual Studio Code.

Code Helper (Plugin).what: A Visual Studio Code extension host.
Code Helper (Plugin).normal: Busy while extensions index or lint.

Code Helper (Renderer).what: A Visual Studio Code window or extension host renderer.
Code Helper (Renderer).normal: Scales with open editors and extensions.
Code Helper (Renderer).check: VS Code, Help, Process Explorer names the extension.

codex.normal: Low CPU while waiting; bursts while it works.
codex.worry: A session you have finished with is still running.

com.apple.accessibility.mediaaccessibili.what: Captions and audio descriptions for media.

com.apple.AmbientDisplayAgent.what: True Tone and ambient light adjustments.

com.apple.AppleUserHIDDrivers.what: User-space drivers for keyboards, mice and trackpads.

com.apple.audio.SandboxHelper.what: Loads audio plug-ins in a sandbox for Core Audio.

com.apple.CloudDocs.iCloudDriveFileProvi.what: The File Provider that presents iCloud Drive in Finder.
com.apple.CloudDocs.iCloudDriveFileProvi.check: Finder, iCloud Drive, and look for items stuck uploading.

com.apple.cmio.registerassistantservice.worry: A virtual camera you did not install.
com.apple.cmio.registerassistantservice.check: System Settings, General, Login Items and Extensions, Camera Extensions.

com.apple.cmio.videodriverkithostextensi.what: Hosts a camera extension (a virtual camera such as OBS or a video app's).
com.apple.cmio.videodriverkithostextensi.normal: Idle unless the virtual camera is in use.
com.apple.cmio.videodriverkithostextensi.worry: Busy when no app should be using the camera.
com.apple.cmio.videodriverkithostextensi.check: System Settings, General, Login Items and Extensions, Camera Extensions.

com.apple.CodeSigningHelper.what: Helper that checks code signatures for other services.

com.apple.dock.extra.what: Dock extras such as the Downloads stack and Handoff icon.

com.apple.DriverKit-AppleBCMWLAN.what: The Wi-Fi chip driver, running in user space (DriverKit).
com.apple.DriverKit-AppleBCMWLAN.normal: Low CPU proportional to Wi-Fi traffic.

com.apple.DriverKit-AppleEthernetE1000.what: A DriverKit driver for Intel-compatible Ethernet, used by virtual machines.

com.apple.DriverKit-IOUserDockChannelSer.what: A DriverKit driver for the dock's serial channel.

com.apple.dt.SKAgent.what: Xcode's SourceKit agent for playgrounds and previews.

com.apple.geod.what: Maps tile and geocoding service used by Maps, Photos and Calendar.
com.apple.geod.normal: Network use while a map is on screen.

com.apple.hiservices-xpcservice.what: Human-interface services: hot keys and menu extras.

com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPr.what: Cleans up after a macOS update.

com.apple.NRD.UpdateBrainService.normal: Network and disk while an update downloads.

com.apple.quicklook.ThumbnailsAgent.what: Generates file thumbnails for Finder and Quick Look.
com.apple.quicklook.ThumbnailsAgent.normal: Busy while browsing folders of images or video.
com.apple.quicklook.ThumbnailsAgent.worry: Constant CPU on one file points at a broken document.

com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine.what: A virtual machine running through Apple's Virtualization framework (Docker, UTM, Parallels-style tools use it).
com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine.normal: CPU and memory proportional to what the VM is doing; the memory figure is the VM's whole allocation.
com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine.worry: High CPU while the VM is meant to be idle.
com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine.check: Look inside the VM; killing this loses its unsaved state.

com.apple.WebKit.GPU.what: GPU process for Safari and WebKit apps.

com.apple.WebKit.Networking.what: Network process for Safari and WebKit apps.

com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.what: A Safari (or any WebKit app) page renderer. One per site group.
com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.normal: Scales with the page: video, ads and web apps are heavy.
com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.worry: One at 100% for a long time is usually a runaway page script or a crypto-mining page.
com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.check: Close the tab; Safari reloads it if needed.

com.docker.build.normal: Busy only during an image build.

com.nordvpn.macos.helper.check: Remove it with NordVPN's uninstaller if you no longer use it.

com.nordvpn.macos.Shield.normal: Low CPU while it filters traffic.

CommCenter.what: Cellular and telephony services, including calls relayed from iPhone.

commerce.normal: Idle unless buying or updating apps.

communicationtrustd.what: Verifies trusted communications for FaceTime and iMessage.

configd.what: Network configuration: interfaces, DNS, proxies, VPN state.

Console.normal: High CPU while streaming a busy log.

contactsd.what: The Contacts database server every app reads contacts through.
contactsd.worry: Constant CPU points at an app hammering the address book.

containermanagerd_system.what: System-wide app container (sandbox data folder) management.

ContainerMetadataExtractor.what: Reads metadata from app containers for Spotlight.

contentlinkingd.what: Links content across apps for Siri and Spotlight.

context7-mcp@latest.what: The Context7 documentation MCP server for an AI assistant.

contextstored.what: Stores the on-device context that Siri and Suggestions read from.

ContinuityCaptureAgent.what: Continuity Camera: use an iPhone as a webcam or scanner.
ContinuityCaptureAgent.normal: Idle unless a camera session is active.

ControlCenter.what: Control Centre and its menu bar items.

Core Audio Driver (ParrotAudioPlugin.dri.what: A third-party Core Audio driver (Parrot headsets).
Core Audio Driver (ParrotAudioPlugin.dri.normal: Idle unless the device is in use.
Core Audio Driver (ParrotAudioPlugin.dri.worry: Present with the device software uninstalled.
Core Audio Driver (ParrotAudioPlugin.dri.check: Remove the driver from /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL if unused.

coreaudiod.what: The audio server. Every app's sound passes through it.
coreaudiod.worry: High CPU with no audio playing suggests an audio plugin or virtual device misbehaving.
coreaudiod.check: Look for third-party audio drivers (virtual cables, loopback devices).

coreautha.what: The per-user LocalAuthentication agent that draws the Touch ID sheet.

coreauthd.what: LocalAuthentication: Touch ID and password prompts for apps.

corebrightnessd.what: Adjusts display brightness, True Tone and Night Shift.

coreduetd.what: Learns your usage patterns to schedule background work and power predictions.
coreduetd.worry: Sustained CPU after a big import (Photos, Mail) is normal for a while.
coreduetd.check: Give it an hour after a migration before worrying.

CoreLocationAgent.what: The per-user side of Location Services that shows the permission prompts.

corerepaird.what: Verifies genuine Apple parts after a repair.

coreservicesd.what: Core Services: file metadata, Launch Services queries and system-wide caches.

CoreServicesUIAgent.what: Shows the dialogs for opening downloaded apps, Gatekeeper warnings and progress bars.
CoreServicesUIAgent.normal: Only busy while a dialog is up.

corespeechd.what: Listens for the Siri wake phrase and handles on-device speech.
corespeechd.normal: Low, steady CPU when Listen for Siri is on.
corespeechd.worry: If you never use Siri, this is CPU you can reclaim.
corespeechd.check: System Settings, Siri, turn off Listen for.

corespotlightd.what: Indexes app-provided content (Mail, Notes, Messages) for Spotlight.

coresymbolicationd.what: Turns addresses in crash reports and samples into function names.
coresymbolicationd.normal: Busy while a report or sample is produced.

CrashReporterSupportHelper.what: Helps prepare crash reports for submission.

Creative Cloud.what: Adobe's Creative Cloud desktop app and its background services.
Creative Cloud.normal: Runs at login even when no Adobe app is open.
Creative Cloud.worry: Not a security concern; a resource one.
Creative Cloud.check: Disable launch at login in its preferences.

cron.what: The classic cron scheduler (launchd runs it only when a crontab exists).
cron.worry: Present when you never set a crontab: something installed one.
cron.check: Run crontab -l for your user; see Persistence for system crontabs.

ctkahp.what: CryptoTokenKit helper for the current user.

ctkd.what: CryptoTokenKit: smart cards, security keys and the Secure Enclave as a token.

curl.normal: Network use for the duration of the download.
curl.worry: A curl you did not start; scripts that fetch and run code often show one.

Cursor.normal: Low CPU; the helpers do the work.

Cursor Helper (Plugin).worry: Sustained high CPU means one extension is busy.

Cursor Helper (Renderer).worry: Sustained high CPU usually comes from an extension.

CursorUIViewService.what: Draws the text cursor and selection handles for some apps.

CVMServer.what: Compiles OpenGL and Metal shaders for the GPU.
CVMServer.normal: Bursts when an app first draws.

dasd.what: Duet Activity Scheduler: decides when background tasks run.

dataaccessd.what: Syncs Mail, Calendar and Contacts with Exchange, Google and other accounts.
dataaccessd.worry: Sustained CPU usually means an account is failing to sync and retrying.
dataaccessd.check: System Settings, Internet Accounts, and look for an account asking for its password.

deleted.what: Purges caches when the disk runs low (the purgeable space Finder reports).
deleted.normal: Idle; bursts when space is tight.

deleted_helper.what: The privileged side of the cache purger.

deno.worry: A deno you cannot trace to something you started.

disclaimer.what: A helper named disclaimer; usually a launcher's confirmation dialog.
disclaimer.worry: One you cannot match to an app.

Discord.normal: Low to moderate CPU; voice channels add more.

Discord Helper (Renderer).normal: Low CPU; animated content raises it.

diskimages-helper.normal: Busy during a mount; verification of a large image takes a while.

diskimagesiod.what: Serves the contents of mounted disk images.
diskimagesiod.check: Eject disk images you have finished with.

DiskUnmountWatcher.what: Watches for volumes being removed without ejecting and warns you.

dmd.what: Device management: applies MDM profiles and restrictions.
dmd.worry: Only if this is not a managed Mac.

Dock.what: The Dock, Mission Control, Launchpad and desktop widgets.
Dock.worry: High CPU usually comes from a widget.
Dock.check: Remove recently added widgets; the Dock relaunches on its own.

Docker.what: Docker Desktop, which runs a Linux virtual machine for containers.
Docker.normal: The VM reserves memory even when idle.
Docker.check: Quit Docker Desktop when not developing.

Docker Desktop.what: The Docker Desktop app and its menu-bar item.
Docker Desktop.normal: Low CPU; the Linux VM (com.docker.backend or a VirtualMachine process) does the real work.

Docker Desktop Helper (GPU).what: GPU process for the Docker Desktop dashboard.

Docker Desktop Helper (Renderer).normal: Low CPU when the window is closed.

DocumentPopoverViewService.what: The title-bar document popover (rename, move, tags).

Documents.what: A process whose name matches a folder; usually an app helper that reports its working directory as its title.
Documents.check: Follow the path and the parent process.

dprivacyd.what: Differential privacy: adds noise to usage data before sharing with Apple.

Dropbox.check: Pause syncing from its menu bar item.

duetexpertd.what: Powers Siri Suggestions: app predictions, suggested contacts, Spotlight ranking.
duetexpertd.normal: Periodic bursts, higher after new data arrives.
duetexpertd.worry: Constant high CPU usually clears after indexing settles.
duetexpertd.check: System Settings, Siri and Spotlight, to turn suggestions off per app.

Electron.what: An app built with Electron (a bundled Chromium plus Node.js). The name means the app did not customise its helper names.
Electron.normal: Electron apps use more memory than native ones.
Electron.worry: Rarely a security concern; look at the publisher.
Electron.check: The inspector's app field names the bundle.

eligibilityd.what: Decides which regional features (for example Apple Intelligence) are available on this Mac.

esbuild.what: The esbuild bundler service, kept alive by Vite and other tools.

fairplayd.what: FairPlay DRM for protected media and apps.
fairplayd.normal: Idle; bursts while playing protected content.

ffmpeg.normal: All cores busy while it runs.
ffmpeg.worry: One you did not start; miners sometimes borrow the name.
ffmpeg.check: Verify the executable path; the real one lives in Homebrew or an app bundle.

Figma.normal: Moderate CPU and GPU while editing a large file.

filecoordinationd.what: Mediates file access between apps and file providers so two processes do not write the same file at once.
filecoordinationd.worry: High CPU alongside fileproviderd points at a syncing provider.

fileproviderd.what: Coordinates cloud file providers (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) with the file system.
fileproviderd.normal: Idle. Busy after large sync changes or a fresh sign-in.
fileproviderd.worry: Hours of high CPU suggests a provider stuck enumerating a large tree.
fileproviderd.check: Open Finder, Locations, and see which provider is syncing; pause it before restarting.

Finder.normal: Low CPU. Busy when copying or when a folder with thousands of items is open.
Finder.worry: Constant high CPU with nothing open often points at a stuck cloud folder or a broken Finder extension.
Finder.check: Relaunch from the Apple menu, Force Quit.

findmybeaconingd.what: Broadcasts the Bluetooth beacon that lets a lost Mac be found while asleep.

findmydeviced.what: Find My Mac: lets the Mac be located, locked or erased from another device.

findmylocateagent.what: The per-user Find My location agent.

Firefox.normal: Low CPU; tabs run in content processes.

followupd.what: Follow-up items in System Settings (for example, finish setting up iCloud).

fontd.what: The font server. Registers fonts and hands them to apps.
fontd.worry: Constant CPU points at a corrupt font being rescanned.

fontworker.what: Scans and validates fonts on behalf of fontd.

fseventsd.what: Records file system change events for Spotlight, Time Machine and apps that watch folders.
fseventsd.normal: Low CPU; more while many files change.

fskitd.what: Hosts user-space file systems (FSKit) such as third-party drivers for exFAT or ext4.
fskitd.normal: Idle unless such a volume is mounted.

GamePolicyAgent.what: The per-user side of Game Mode.

gamepolicyd.what: Game Mode: prioritises a full-screen game.

GenerativeExperiencesSafetyInferenceProv.what: Safety checks for Apple Intelligence generation.

geodMachServiceBridge.what: Bridge to the Maps geocoding service.

git.normal: Bursts; a large clone or gc runs longer.
git.worry: A git that never finishes is usually waiting for a credential or a lock.
git.check: Look at the terminal that started it.

go.what: The Go toolchain (build, test or run).

Google Chrome.what: Google's browser. The browser process coordinates many helper processes.
Google Chrome.normal: Low itself; helpers do the work.
Google Chrome.check: Use Chrome's own Task Manager (Window menu) to find the heavy tab or extension.

Google Chrome Helper.what: A Chrome utility process: network service, audio, storage.
Google Chrome Helper.check: Chrome's own Task Manager (Window menu) names each helper.

Google Chrome Helper (GPU).what: Chrome's GPU process: compositing and video decode for every tab.

Google Chrome Helper (Plugin).what: A Chrome plugin or utility process.

Google Chrome Helper (Renderer).what: A Chrome tab or extension renderer. Sandboxed; one per site.
Google Chrome Helper (Renderer).worry: One at 100% for a long time: a runaway page or extension.
Google Chrome Helper (Renderer).check: Chrome's Task Manager shows which tab it is; closing the tab is cleaner than killing.

Google Drive.normal: Network and CPU while syncing; idle otherwise.

gopls.what: The Go language server used by editors.

heard.what: Hearing features: Live Listen and headphone accommodations.

helpd.what: The Help menu's search and help books.

hidd.what: Human interface devices: keyboard, mouse, trackpad.

homed.what: HomeKit: keeps home accessories and automations in sync.

iconservicesagent.what: Renders and caches app and file icons.

iconservicesd.what: Renders and caches icons for Finder and the Dock.
iconservicesd.normal: Bursts when browsing folders with many custom icons.

identityservicesd.what: iMessage and FaceTime identity and registration.

IFTranscriptSELFIngestor.what: Ingests transcripts for Apple Intelligence features.

imagent.what: The iMessage and FaceTime transport agent.

IMAutomaticHistoryDeletionAgent.what: Deletes old messages when Keep Messages is set to 30 days or a year.

IMDPersistenceAgent.worry: Constant CPU points at a large chat being reindexed.

imklaunchagent.what: Launches input methods (for example Japanese or Chinese keyboards).

IMTransferAgent.normal: Network while sending or receiving attachments.

installd.worry: Busy with no install in progress points at a stuck installer.

installerauthagent.what: Handles the password prompt for installers.

intelligenceflowd.what: Coordinates Apple Intelligence requests between apps and the on-device models.
intelligenceflowd.normal: Idle; bursts while a request runs.
intelligenceflowd.worry: Sustained CPU after an Apple Intelligence feature stops being used.
intelligenceflowd.check: System Settings, Apple Intelligence and Siri.

IOMFB_bics_daemon.what: Display-panel calibration and brightness for built-in screens.

IOUserBluetoothSerialDriver.what: A DriverKit driver for Bluetooth serial devices.

IPNExtension.what: Tailscale's network extension: the part that actually routes packets.
IPNExtension.normal: Low CPU proportional to VPN traffic.

iStat Menus.normal: A few percent CPU; that is the cost of polling sensors.

java.what: A Java virtual machine. IDEs, build tools and servers run in it.
java.normal: Memory in the hundreds of megabytes is normal; CPU depends on the app.
java.worry: A java you cannot trace to an app.
java.check: Sample it to see the main class.

karabiner_grabber.what: Karabiner-Elements' privileged keyboard grabber. It sees every keystroke.
karabiner_grabber.worry: Present with Karabiner uninstalled: something is reading keystrokes.
karabiner_grabber.check: Uninstall Karabiner properly if you no longer use it.

kernel_task.what: The kernel itself, shown as a process. It also throttles CPU to control temperature by taking cycles for itself.
kernel_task.normal: Low CPU. High CPU when the Mac is hot or on a weak charger is deliberate thermal throttling.
kernel_task.worry: Sustained high CPU while the Mac is cool can indicate a misbehaving driver or a blocked fan.
kernel_task.check: Check temperature and the power adapter; look for a kernel extension or system extension you installed recently.

KernelEventAgent.what: Relays kernel events (for example a full disk or an unmounted network volume) to the user.

keybagd.what: Manages the keybag that protects Data Protection class keys.

Keychain Circle Notification.what: Prompts for iCloud Keychain approval from another device.

knowledge-agent.what: Learns usage patterns for Siri Suggestions and Screen Time.

launchd.what: The first process. Starts and supervises every other daemon and agent, and relaunches the ones that must stay up.
launchd.worry: Never itself; look at what it launched.

launchservicesd.what: Launch Services: which app opens which file type and URL.

ld.what: The linker, run at the end of a build.

limactl.what: Lima: Linux virtual machines on macOS (used by Colima and Rancher Desktop).

liveactivitiesd.what: Live Activities from iPhone shown on the Mac.

locationd.what: Location Services: works out where the Mac is from Wi-Fi and asks your permission on behalf of apps.
locationd.normal: Idle; bursts when an app asks for location.
locationd.worry: Constant CPU means an app is polling location continuously.
locationd.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Location Services shows which apps used it recently.

lockoutagent.what: Enforces the screen lock after failed attempts.

logd.what: The unified logging daemon. Collects log messages from every process.
logd.normal: Low CPU. Higher when something logs excessively.
logd.worry: Sustained CPU means a process is spamming the log.
logd.check: Open Console and see which process is most verbose.

logd_helper.what: Privileged helper for the unified logging daemon.

Logi Options+.worry: Constant CPU is a known problem with some versions.
Logi Options+.check: Update it, or quit it from the menu bar.

logind.what: Tracks login sessions and the console user.

loginwindow.what: Manages the login session: login, logout, lock screen.

logioptionsplus_agent.worry: Constant CPU is a known problem with some versions.

Loom.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Screen and System Audio Recording.

lsd.what: Launch Services database: which app opens which file type and URL scheme.
lsd.normal: Idle; brief bursts after installing an app.

Mail.normal: Low CPU; bursts while indexing new mail.
Mail.worry: Sustained CPU points at an account resyncing.

managedcorespotlightd.what: Spotlight indexing for managed (MDM) app data.

ManagedSettingsAgent.what: Applies Screen Time restrictions to apps.

mapssyncd.what: Syncs Maps favourites and recents through iCloud.

mcp-server-supabase@latest.what: The Supabase MCP server for an AI assistant.
mcp-server-supabase@latest.normal: Idle; network when it queries your project.
mcp-server-supabase@latest.worry: Its access token is often passed on the command line, where every local process can read it.
mcp-server-supabase@latest.check: Move the token to an environment variable in the MCP configuration.

mcp@latest.what: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server launched through npx for an AI assistant.
mcp@latest.worry: One that outlives the assistant that started it, or one launched with secrets in its arguments (visible to every local process).
mcp@latest.check: Follow the parent to see which assistant owns it; prefer environment variables to command-line tokens.

mdbulkimport.what: Imports many files into the Spotlight index at once, usually after a migration or a new volume.
mdbulkimport.normal: High CPU for a while after a big change; then gone.
mdbulkimport.worry: Only if it runs for days.
mdbulkimport.check: System Settings, Siri and Spotlight, Spotlight Privacy, to exclude a busy folder.

mDNSResponder.what: DNS resolution and Bonjour discovery for every process.
mDNSResponder.worry: Sustained CPU can mean an app is flooding DNS lookups.
mDNSResponder.check: Restarting it drops DNS caches; harmless.

mds.what: The Spotlight metadata server. Schedules indexing and answers searches.
mds.normal: Bursts after files change; heavy for hours after a migration or a large download.
mds.check: System Settings, Siri & Spotlight, Spotlight Privacy: exclude the folder that keeps changing.

mdworker.what: A Spotlight indexing worker. Reads a file and extracts its metadata; many run in parallel.
mdworker.worry: Dozens at once for a long time: something is generating files continuously.

mdworker_shared.what: A shared Spotlight indexing worker used for common file types.

mediaanalysisd.what: Analyses photos and video for faces, objects, Live Text and scene search.
mediaanalysisd.normal: Heavy CPU for hours after a large photo import, when the Mac is idle and on power.
mediaanalysisd.worry: Only if it never settles across days.
mediaanalysisd.check: Leave the Mac plugged in overnight.

mediaremoteagent.what: The per-user side of Now Playing.

mediaremoted.what: Now Playing: routes play and pause between apps and the media keys.

metrickitd.what: Collects performance metrics that apps can request through MetricKit.

Microsoft AutoUpdate.what: Microsoft's updater for Office and Edge.

Microsoft Defender.worry: Sustained high CPU on file-heavy work (builds, git) is a known cost; exclude build folders.

Microsoft Edge Helper (Renderer).worry: One at high CPU is a heavy page.

Microsoft Excel.normal: Low CPU; high while recalculating a big workbook.

Microsoft Outlook.normal: Low CPU; bursts while syncing mail.
Microsoft Outlook.worry: Sustained CPU points at a mailbox resync.

Microsoft Teams.what: Microsoft Teams (an Electron or WebView app).
Microsoft Teams.normal: Heavy during calls and screen sharing.
Microsoft Teams.check: Quit when not in a call.

Microsoft Word.normal: Low CPU; spikes on large documents.

milod.what: Motion and sensor data for Focus and activity features.

mlhostd.what: Hosts machine-learning model execution for system features.

mobileactivationd.what: Activation with Apple's servers for Activation Lock.

mobileassetd.what: Downloads system assets: dictation models, fonts, XProtect definitions, Siri voices.
mobileassetd.normal: Bursts after updates or first use of a feature.

modelcatalogd.what: The catalogue of on-device models and their versions.

modelmanagerd.what: Downloads and manages the on-device machine-learning models Apple Intelligence uses.
modelmanagerd.normal: Bursts of network and disk after updates.
modelmanagerd.worry: Constant download traffic that never finishes.
modelmanagerd.check: Let it finish on a good connection.

mongod.worry: One listening on a network interface.
mongod.check: The Network tab shows whether it is bound to localhost only.

mscamerad-xpc.what: Continuity Camera: uses an iPhone as a webcam.

Music.normal: Low CPU while playing; more while syncing a large library.

mysqld.worry: One listening on a network interface.
mysqld.check: The Network tab shows whether it is bound to localhost only.

naturallanguaged.what: Natural-language processing shared by Mail, Notes and Spotlight.

neagent.what: Hosts a Network Extension (a VPN or content filter) for the current user.
neagent.normal: Low CPU; network traffic passes through it.
neagent.worry: A neagent you do not recognise means a VPN or filter you did not knowingly install.
neagent.check: System Settings, Network, VPN and Filters.

nearbyd.what: Ultra-wideband and proximity for AirDrop, AirTag and Find My.

nehelper.what: Network Extension helper: manages VPN, content filter and DNS proxy extensions.
nehelper.worry: Rarely itself; it is how VPN apps and filters get their hooks in.
nehelper.check: System Settings, Network, VPN and Filters shows what is installed.

netbiosd.what: Announces the Mac on Windows networks (NetBIOS) for file sharing.
netbiosd.check: System Settings, General, Sharing, File Sharing, Options.

networkserviceproxy.what: Routes iCloud Private Relay and some Apple services through Apple's relays.
networkserviceproxy.normal: Network traffic when Private Relay is on.
networkserviceproxy.check: System Settings, your Apple ID, iCloud, Private Relay.

newsd.what: Fetches and indexes Apple News content.
newsd.normal: Network bursts while News is open or refreshing.

next-server.normal: Low CPU; bursts on each request and rebuild.
next-server.worry: A forgotten dev server; check which port it holds.
next-server.check: The Network tab shows its port.

nfcd.what: NFC for Apple Pay and tags.

NFStorageServer.what: Storage for Notes and similar apps' file attachments.

nginx.worry: One you did not start, or one bound to all interfaces.
nginx.check: The Network tab shows its listeners.

node.what: A Node.js runtime running some script or server. The parent process says which tool started it.
node.worry: A node process you did not start, from an unusual location, deserves a look.
node.check: Inspect the parent chain and the path; developer tools spawn many of these.

node_repl.what: A Node.js REPL or an inspector session.

NotificationCenter.what: Notifications and the Notification Centre panel.

notifyd.what: The system notification bus. Processes post and listen for named events through it (this is not the banners you see on screen).
notifyd.worry: Rarely; a chatty client can make it busy, but the client is the culprit.

npm.what: The npm package manager or a script it started.
npm.normal: Bursts during installs; a dev server runs as long as you keep it.

NRDUpdated.normal: Idle unless an update is pending.

nsattributedstringagent.what: Renders rich text (for example HTML) for apps in a separate process.

nsurlsessiond.what: Background downloads and uploads on behalf of apps and system services.
nsurlsessiond.normal: Busy during updates, iCloud sync and app downloads.
nsurlsessiond.worry: Sustained heavy traffic with nothing you started: find the app using it.
nsurlsessiond.check: Look at the network trace on the scope and at which app is active.

ntpd.what: A network time daemon (not Apple's; Apple uses timed).

oahd.what: Rosetta 2: translates Intel-only apps so they run on Apple silicon.
oahd.normal: A burst the first time an Intel binary runs, then idle.
oahd.worry: Constant CPU means an Intel app is being retranslated or is itself busy; the app is the culprit.
oahd.check: Find the process marked Intel and look for an Apple silicon version.

OBS.normal: High CPU and GPU while streaming or recording.

ollama.normal: Idle when no model is loaded; heavy CPU or GPU and memory in the gigabytes while a model runs.
ollama.worry: Memory held after you have finished; models stay loaded for a while by default.
ollama.check: Quit the Ollama menu-bar app to free the memory.

OneDrive.check: Pause syncing from its menu bar item.

opendirectoryd.what: User accounts, groups and directory lookups (local and network).

osanalyticshelper.what: Collects analytics logs for Apple and app developers.
osanalyticshelper.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Analytics and Improvements.

ospredictiond.what: Predicts when the system is idle enough for background tasks.

PAH_Extension.what: A Personal Audio Hosting extension: hosts AudioUnit v3 plug-ins out of process.
PAH_Extension.normal: Low CPU while an audio app uses the plug-in.

parsecd.what: Spotlight Suggestions and Safari Suggestions from Apple.
parsecd.normal: Network while typing in Spotlight or Safari's address bar.
parsecd.worry: If you would rather searches stayed local, turn suggestions off.
parsecd.check: System Settings, Siri and Spotlight, Spotlight, Siri Suggestions.

PasswordBreachAgent.what: Checks saved passwords against known breaches for the Passwords app.

pboard.what: The clipboard server. Every copy and paste goes through it.
pboard.worry: Never itself; a clipboard manager polling it would show as that app.

pbs.what: Pasteboard services: builds the Services menu from installed apps.
pbs.normal: Brief bursts after installing an app.

peopled.what: Builds the People album in Photos from face recognition.

periodic.what: Runs the daily, weekly and monthly maintenance scripts.

photoanalysisd.what: Analyses the Photos library for faces, scenes and memories.
photoanalysisd.normal: High CPU for hours after importing photos, usually when the Mac is idle and plugged in.

photolibraryd.normal: Busy while Photos is open or syncing.

Photos.normal: Heavy CPU after an import while it analyses images; low otherwise.

pkd.what: Plug-in kit: discovers and launches app extensions (share sheet, widgets, Finder sync).

plugin-container.what: A Firefox content, GPU or extension process.
plugin-container.worry: One at high CPU is a heavy page or extension.

PlugInLibraryService.what: Loads plug-ins for apps in a separate process.

pnpm.what: The pnpm package manager or a script it started.

PnROnDeviceWorker.what: On-device summarisation and rewriting for Apple Intelligence.

postgres.normal: Low CPU when idle; memory for shared buffers.
postgres.worry: A postgres you did not install, or one listening on a network interface.
postgres.check: The Network tab shows whether it is bound to localhost only.

powerexperienced.what: Low Power Mode and power-related notifications.

Preview.what: The Preview app for images and PDFs.
Preview.normal: Low CPU; spikes when rendering a large PDF.

prl_vm_app.normal: CPU and memory proportional to the guest.
prl_vm_app.check: Shut the guest down from inside.

proactived.what: Another Siri Suggestions worker: proposes events, contacts and apps from what you do.

ptpcamerad.what: Talks to cameras and phones in picture-transfer mode.
ptpcamerad.normal: Idle unless a camera is connected.

python.what: A Python interpreter. Tools, notebooks, MCP servers and scripts run inside it.
python.worry: A python you cannot trace to a script or tool you started.
python.check: Sample it to see the script path, or follow the parent process.

python3.what: A Python interpreter running a script.
python3.worry: A Python process from Downloads or a temp folder that you did not start deserves a look.
python3.check: Inspect the parent chain and the path.

qemu-system-aarch64.what: A QEMU virtual machine (UTM, Lima, Android emulator).
qemu-system-aarch64.normal: CPU and memory proportional to the guest.
qemu-system-aarch64.worry: High CPU while the guest is idle.
qemu-system-aarch64.check: Shut the guest down from inside; killing loses its state.

QLPreviewGenerationExtension.what: Renders a Quick Look preview for one document type.
QLPreviewGenerationExtension.normal: Alive while a preview is open.

rapportd.what: Device-to-device communication for Continuity features (Universal Control, Sidecar, Handoff).
rapportd.normal: Idle. It listens on a network port for nearby Apple devices.

Raycast.normal: Low CPU; bursts while its extensions run.
Raycast.worry: Sustained CPU points at a busy extension or script command.

recentsd.what: Tracks recent contacts and documents for suggestions.

redis-server.worry: One listening on a network interface without a password.
redis-server.check: The Network tab shows whether it is bound to localhost only.

remindd.what: The Reminders database and sync agent.

remoted.what: Remote device pairing for Xcode and Apple's own remote services.

replayd.what: Screen recording and screen sharing capture.
replayd.normal: Busy only while recording or sharing the screen.
replayd.worry: Busy when you are not recording means something is capturing your screen.
replayd.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Screen and System Audio Recording.

replicatord.what: Replicates data between paired Apple devices.

ReportCrash.what: Writes a crash report when a process dies with a signal.
ReportCrash.worry: Seeing it often means something keeps crashing.
ReportCrash.check: Console, Crash Reports, to see what crashed.

ReportSystemMemory.what: Writes a memory report when the system is under memory pressure.
ReportSystemMemory.normal: Runs briefly, and only when memory is tight.
ReportSystemMemory.worry: Seeing it often means memory is genuinely short.
ReportSystemMemory.check: Sort by memory and close the largest apps.

revisiond.what: Stores document versions for apps that support Revert To.

routined.what: Significant Locations: learns places you visit for Maps and Siri.
routined.worry: If you would rather it did not, turn it off.
routined.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Location Services, System Services, Significant Locations.

rtcreportingd.what: Reports FaceTime and iMessage call quality to Apple.

runningboardd.what: Tracks process lifecycle and resource limits for apps and extensions.

rust-analyzer.what: The Rust language server used by editors.
rust-analyzer.normal: Heavy CPU while indexing a crate; then low.

SAExtensionOrchestrator.what: Orchestrates on-device Siri and Apple Intelligence extensions.

Safari.what: Apple's web browser. Page content runs in separate WebContent processes.
Safari.normal: Low CPU itself; the WebContent processes do the work.
Safari.check: Close heavy tabs; look at com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.

SafariBookmarksSyncAgent.what: Syncs Safari bookmarks and tabs through iCloud.

SafariLaunchAgent.what: Safari background tasks such as Reading List downloads.

sandboxd.what: Reports App Sandbox violations to the log.

ScopedBookmarkAgent.what: Resolves security-scoped bookmarks so sandboxed apps can reopen files you granted.

screensharingd.what: Apple's Screen Sharing and Remote Management server.
screensharingd.worry: Busy when nobody should be connected.
screensharingd.check: System Settings, General, Sharing, Screen Sharing.

ScreenTimeAgent.what: Tracks app usage for Screen Time and enforces its limits.

searchpartyd.what: The Find My network daemon: reports nearby AirTags and lets this Mac be found.
searchpartyd.check: System Settings, your Apple ID, iCloud, Find My Mac.

searchpartyuseragent.what: The per-user side of the Find My network.

secd.what: The keychain and Secure Enclave access daemon.

secinitd.what: Initialises the sandbox and security context for new processes.

securityd_system.what: The system-context security server for keychain and trust before login.

server-github.what: The GitHub MCP server for an AI assistant.

server-memory.what: The memory MCP server for an AI assistant.

server-sequential-thinking.what: The sequential-thinking MCP server for an AI assistant.

ServiceExtension.worry: Rarely; the parent app tells you what it is for.

seserviced.what: Secure Element services for Apple Pay.

SetStoreUpdateService.what: Updates the App Store's local catalogue.

sh.what: The POSIX shell, used by scripts and by tools that spawn commands.
sh.worry: A long-lived sh at high CPU is a script in a loop.

shadcn-ui-mcp-server.what: The shadcn/ui MCP server for an AI assistant.

sharedfilelistd.what: Keeps the Recent Items and login-items lists.

ShareSheetUI.normal: Alive while a share sheet is open.

sharingd.what: AirDrop, Handoff, Continuity and shared clipboard.
sharingd.check: Turn AirDrop to Contacts Only or Off if you never use it.

ShortcutsViewService.what: Renders Shortcuts UI inside other apps.

SidecarRelay.what: Sidecar: uses an iPad as a display.

simdiskimaged.what: Mounts simulator runtime disk images for Xcode.

SimLaunchHost.arm64.what: Launches apps in the iOS Simulator.
SimLaunchHost.arm64.normal: Idle unless a simulator is running.

siriactionsd.what: Runs Shortcuts and Siri actions in the background.
siriactionsd.normal: Idle unless a shortcut is running.
siriactionsd.worry: Constant CPU means an automation is looping.
siriactionsd.check: Open Shortcuts and look at Automation.

SiriUploadWorker.what: Uploads Siri analytics when sharing is on.
SiriUploadWorker.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Analytics and Improvements.

SkyComputerUseService.what: A computer-use automation service for an AI assistant (Sky). It can see the screen and control apps.
SkyComputerUseService.worry: Busy when you have not asked for an automation.
SkyComputerUseService.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Accessibility and Screen Recording.

Slack.what: The Slack desktop app's main process.
Slack.normal: Low CPU; renderers do the work.

Slack Helper (Renderer).what: A Slack window renderer (Slack is an Electron app).

sleep.what: The sleep command: a script waiting for a timer.

smd.what: Service Management: registers login items and privileged helpers.

socketfilterfw.what: The application firewall. Decides which apps may accept incoming connections.
socketfilterfw.worry: Absent while the firewall is shown as on.

softwareupdated.what: Checks for and downloads macOS updates.
softwareupdated.normal: Bursts; heavy while downloading an update.

SoftwareUpdateNotificationManager.what: Shows the update-available badge and notifications.

SourceKitService.what: Xcode's Swift language service: indexing, completion, diagnostics.
SourceKitService.normal: Heavy CPU while indexing a project; then low.
SourceKitService.worry: Constant high CPU on a small project points at a stuck index.
SourceKitService.check: Quit Xcode and delete DerivedData if it never settles.

Spotify Helper.what: A Spotify helper process (renderer or GPU).

spotlightknowledged.what: Builds Spotlight's knowledge index over your documents and messages.

ssh.what: An SSH client session to another machine (or a tunnel).
ssh.normal: Low CPU; traffic proportional to what passes through.
ssh.worry: A session you did not open, or an outbound connection to a host you do not recognise.
ssh.check: The Network tab shows the remote host.

ssh-agent.what: Holds decrypted SSH keys for the session so you do not retype passphrases.

sshd.what: The SSH server. Present when Remote Login is on.
sshd.worry: If you did not enable Remote Login, turn it off.
sshd.check: System Settings, General, Sharing, Remote Login.

storagekitd.what: Disk Utility's back end: partitions, APFS volumes, disk images.
storagekitd.normal: Busy only while Disk Utility works.

SubmitDiagInfo.what: Sends diagnostics to Apple when analytics sharing is on.
SubmitDiagInfo.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Analytics and Improvements.

suggestd.what: Extracts contacts, events and suggestions from Mail and Messages.

suhelperd.what: The privileged helper for Software Update.

swift-frontend.what: The Swift compiler, one per file being compiled.
swift-frontend.normal: High CPU during a build; gone afterwards.

swtransparencyd.what: Software transparency: verifies signed logs of Apple software versions.

syncdefaultsd.what: Syncs preferences through iCloud (the ubiquity key-value store).

sysextd.what: Installs and runs system extensions (the modern replacement for kernel extensions).
sysextd.worry: Never itself; the extensions it hosts show separately.
sysextd.check: System Settings, General, Login Items and Extensions.

syslogd.what: The legacy system logger. Most logging now goes through logd, but syslogd still handles the old BSD path.
syslogd.worry: High CPU means something is writing log lines in a loop.
syslogd.check: Read /var/log/system.log for the repeating line and find its sender.

sysmond.what: Serves per-process statistics to Activity Monitor and similar tools.
sysmond.normal: Idle unless a monitor is open; a few percent while one polls.
sysmond.worry: Never itself; it is busy because a monitor asked.
sysmond.check: Close monitoring apps you are not using.

syspolicyd.what: Gatekeeper's policy engine. Decides whether downloaded software may run.
syspolicyd.normal: Bursts when an app first launches.

system_installd.what: Installs the parts of an update that go into the sealed system volume.

systemstats.what: Collects power and usage statistics for the battery menu and Apple's diagnostics.
systemstats.normal: Brief periodic work; near-zero on average.
systemstats.worry: Sustained CPU is unusual and usually clears after a restart.

systemstatusd.what: System status indicators such as the orange microphone dot.

SystemUIServer.what: Menu bar extras and system menus.
SystemUIServer.worry: A third-party menu bar item can keep it busy.
SystemUIServer.check: Quit menu bar apps one at a time.

tail.what: The tail command, usually following a log.

Tailscale.normal: Low CPU; encrypted traffic to your tailnet.

talagentd.what: Transparent App Lifecycle: saves and restores window state for Resume.

taskgated.what: Decides which processes may be debugged or attached to.

tccd.what: Privacy permissions (camera, microphone, screen recording, Full Disk Access).

TeamViewer.normal: Idle unless a session is active.
TeamViewer.worry: A session active when you are not using it means someone else is.
TeamViewer.check: Quit it when not in use; review its connection log.

Terminal.normal: Idle unless a command is running.

textunderstandingd.what: Recognises dates, addresses and the like in text for data detectors.

TGOnDeviceInferenceProviderService.what: On-device text generation for Writing Tools.
TGOnDeviceInferenceProviderService.normal: Bursts while a Writing Tools request runs.

thermalmonitord.what: Watches temperature sensors and tells the system when to throttle.
thermalmonitord.worry: Never itself; if the Mac is throttling, find the hot process.
thermalmonitord.check: Sort by CPU and look at kernel_task.

timed.what: Keeps the clock in sync with Apple's time servers.
timed.worry: If the clock drifts, this is what to look at, not a process to kill.
timed.check: System Settings, General, Date and Time.

tmux.check: Killing it closes every session inside.

triald.what: Apple's on-device experiments framework: fetches feature-flag configurations.

triald_system.what: The system-wide side of Apple's experiments framework.

trustd.what: Evaluates certificate trust for TLS connections and code signing.
trustd.normal: Small bursts whenever apps open connections.
trustd.worry: Constant CPU can indicate a certificate revocation check that keeps failing.
trustd.check: Check the network; a captive portal or a broken proxy makes it retry.

trustdFileHelper.what: Helper for trustd that reads certificate files.

uarpassetmanagerd.what: Firmware updates for accessories (AirPods, Studio Display, Magic keyboards).
uarpassetmanagerd.normal: Idle; bursts when an accessory updates.

UIKitSystem.what: Supports iPhone and iPad apps running on the Mac.

universalAccessAuthWarn.what: Warns when an app asks for Accessibility control.

UniversalControl.what: Universal Control: one keyboard and mouse across Macs and iPads.

Updater.normal: Brief network use when it checks for updates.
Updater.worry: An updater with no matching app installed.
Updater.check: Follow the path to the app that owns it.

UsageTrackingAgent.what: Records app and website usage for Screen Time.

usbaudiod.normal: Low CPU while a USB audio device is in use.

usbmuxd.what: Multiplexes connections to iPhones and iPads over USB and Wi-Fi.

useractivityd.what: Handoff: advertises what you are doing so your other devices can continue it.

UserEventAgent.what: Runs the system's event-driven plug-ins: network reachability changes, disk mounts, time zone changes, and similar triggers for launchd jobs.
UserEventAgent.normal: Near-zero CPU; short spikes when the network or a volume changes.
UserEventAgent.worry: Constant CPU points at a plug-in looping on an event, often a third-party VPN or backup agent.
UserEventAgent.check: Look for a third-party bundle under /Library/UserEventPlugins.

usermanagerd.what: Tracks which users are logged in and switches between them.

usernoted.what: Stores notifications and their settings for Notification Centre.

UserNotificationCenter.what: Shows system alerts that need an answer, such as a disk that could not be ejected.
UserNotificationCenter.normal: Only alive while a dialog is up.

usernotificationsd.what: Delivers notifications from apps to Notification Centre.

uv.what: The uv Python package manager and runner; it usually launches a Python tool.
uv.normal: Brief; the Python it launches does the work.

UVCAssistant.normal: Low CPU while a webcam is in use.
UVCAssistant.worry: Busy with no video app open means something has the camera.
UVCAssistant.check: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Camera.

ViewBridgeAuxiliary.what: Hosts remote views (file dialogs, share sheets) drawn in another process.

VMware Fusion.normal: CPU and memory proportional to the guest.
VMware Fusion.check: Shut the guest down from inside.

WallpaperAerialsExtension.what: Downloads and plays the aerial wallpapers and screen savers.
WallpaperAerialsExtension.normal: Network while downloading; GPU while playing.
WallpaperAerialsExtension.worry: Repeated large downloads; they are hundreds of megabytes each.
WallpaperAerialsExtension.check: System Settings, Wallpaper, to remove downloaded aerials.

WallpaperAgent.what: Renders the desktop wallpaper, including the aerial and dynamic ones.
WallpaperAgent.normal: Bursts when the wallpaper changes; aerials use the GPU while playing.
WallpaperAgent.worry: Constant CPU on a static wallpaper.
WallpaperAgent.check: Switch to a still wallpaper to test.

watchdogd.what: Pets the hardware watchdog so the machine restarts if the kernel hangs.

wdavdaemon.normal: Low CPU; high during scans and file-heavy work.

wget.worry: A wget you did not start.

WiFiAgent.what: The per-user Wi-Fi agent behind the menu bar item and join prompts.

wifip2pd.what: Peer-to-peer Wi-Fi for AirDrop and Continuity.

WindowServer.what: Composites every window on screen and handles input. Every app's drawing goes through it.
WindowServer.normal: Scales with what is on screen: animations, many windows, external displays, screen recording.
WindowServer.worry: Sustained high CPU with nothing moving on screen usually means an app is redrawing constantly.
WindowServer.check: Find the app with high CPU alongside it; close windows or disable transparency in Accessibility settings.

WirelessRadioManagerd.what: Coordinates Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios so they do not interfere.

Xcode.worry: Sustained CPU after a build finishes usually means indexing a large project.

XProtectBridgeService.what: Bridges XProtect Remediator with the rest of the system.

xprotectd.what: Coordinates XProtect malware scans and remediations.

XprotectRemediator.what: Apple's background malware removal tool. Scans for and removes known threats.

XProtectService.what: Apple's built-in malware scanner, run on demand.
XProtectService.normal: Bursts when apps launch or files are downloaded.

yarn.what: The yarn package manager or a script it started.

zoom.us.worry: Check its screen-recording and microphone permissions in the Privacy scan.
zoom.us.check: Quit when not in a call.

zsh.what: The default shell. Each terminal tab has one; scripts and tool launchers often start one too.
zsh.normal: Idle while waiting for you to type.
zsh.worry: A zsh at high CPU is running a script or a loop; the child process is usually the real work.
zsh.check: Look at its children in the Processes tab.
